question.text:
Consider the following logical sentences. For each sentence, comment on its validity and satisfiability:

1. (Smoke $\rightarrow$ Fire $) \rightarrow(\neg$ Smoke $\rightarrow \neg$ Fire $)$

2. $(($ Smoke $\wedge$ Heat $) \rightarrow$ Fire $) \leftrightarrow(($ Smoke $\rightarrow$ Fire $) \vee($ Heat $\rightarrow$ Fire $))$

3. $B i g \vee D u m b \vee(B i g \rightarrow D u m b)$

4. $($ Big $\wedge$ Dumb $) \vee \neg$ Dumb

Which of the following is correct?

A. 1 and 2 are valid; 3 and 4 are satisfiable but not valid.

B. 2 and 3 are valid; 1 and 4 are satisfiable but not valid.

C. $1, 2, 3$ are valid; 4 is satisfiable but not valid.

D. $1, 2, 3$, and 4 are all valid.
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Which of the following is a correct predicate logic statement for "Every Natural number has one successor"?

A. $\forall x \exists y(\operatorname{succ}(x, y) \wedge(\exists z \operatorname{succ}(x, z) \Rightarrow \operatorname{equal}(y, z)))$

B. $\forall x \exists y(\operatorname{succ}(x, y) \vee(\exists z \operatorname{succ}(x, z) \Rightarrow \operatorname{equal}(y, z)))$

C. $\exists x \forall y(\operatorname{succ}(x, y) \wedge(\exists z \operatorname{succ}(x, z) \Rightarrow \operatorname{equal}(y, z)))$

D. $\forall x \exists y(\operatorname{succ}(x, y))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:

$$
[(p \rightarrow q) \wedge(r \rightarrow \neg q)] \rightarrow(r \rightarrow \neg p)
$$

If the formula is a tautology, submit your answer as $\mathbf{1}$. If it is not a tautology, submit your answer as $\mathbf{0}$

question.text:
Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer from the code given below :

\[
\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
\text{} & \text{List I} & \text{} & \text{List II} \\
\hline
(a) & \text{Equivalence} & (i) & p \Rightarrow q \\
\hline
(b) & \text{Contrapositive} & (ii) & p \Rightarrow q ; q \Rightarrow p \\
\hline
(c) & \text{Converse} & (iii) & p \Rightarrow q : \sim q \Rightarrow \sim p \\
\hline
(d) & \text{Implication} & (iv) & p \Leftrightarrow q \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

A. (a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iii), (d)-(iv)

B. (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iii), (d)-(iv)

C. (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)

D. (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
The first order logic (FOL) statement $((R \vee Q) \wedge(P \vee \neg Q))$ is equivalent to which of the following?

A. $((R \vee \neg Q) \wedge(P \vee \neg Q) \wedge(R \vee P))$

B. $((R \vee Q) \wedge(P \vee \neg Q) \wedge(R \vee P))$

C. $((R \vee Q) \wedge(P \vee \neg Q) \wedge(R \vee \neg P))$

D. $((R \vee Q) \wedge(P \vee \neg Q) \wedge(\neg R \vee P))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic
